projectSpecificInferences: Simple fish could use a locally weighted body/tail chain with the head pinned, plus fin meshes; this differs from translating or rotating the complete PNG.
Turtles, rays and jellyfish need anatomy-specific fin/flipper/tentacle masks and independent deform controls; one universal sine warp is insufficient evidence of correct action.
Flattened octopus arms and curled dragon bodies contain overlap; independent moving parts can reveal unpainted hidden pixels, requiring separated/AI-repaired native layers.
Guide blink, pointing and new hand or sleeve poses need alternate native image content for closed eyelids and newly revealed surfaces; mesh interpolation cannot invent that art.
Boss tell/attack/recovery and enraged expressions need authored distinct action phases; reusing the swim warp with larger amplitude is not a completed attack.
Texture deformation preserves the source colour information but resamples it during rendering. It is derived raster animation, not newly generated native detail or a video model output.
minimumPrototypePlan: Keep one accepted identity master and hash per creature.
Author explicit head/body/tail/fin mesh boundaries and local weights; pin the identity region and shared root.
Check no inverted triangles, no silhouette clipping, no alpha holes and no hidden-part exposure.
Render fixed source canvases, review visible actual appendage movement at game scale over light/dark backgrounds.
Check loop seam and one-shot recovery and then package frame timing, anchors, source relationships and runtime integration.
Do not alter existing video-only acceptance status until the replacement art method and each action are actually produced and reviewed.
